I first played Darksiders on the PS3 years ago, but never got a chance to finish it. I finally did, and am just starting on Darksiders II. I wanted to share my observations, and see if others feel the same way about the games as I do;

Darksiders always seemed to have the "you are in the middle of hell on earth" atmosphere down pat. It didn't matter what area you were in, it always felt like some scary shit was right behind you, or was about to be. War, the protagonist, seemed like he would be slow and lumbering, but instead he played bulky, yet fluid and nimble. For that I applaud the character development team. Even his dialogue was spot on. I don't expect a horseman of the apocalypse to be a man of many words, and I glad they did not make him this way.

The only real issue I had with this game ties to the version I finally completed it with; the Warmastered Edition. It has a major bug with cut-scene skips that is incredibly frustrating. Case in point; I finally play all the way through Darksiders and make it to the very end. I beat the end boss and......no end cinematic, just credits. I had to watch the fucking ending on youtube, because not only does it have this "fuck you" bug in place, they didn't bother to add in a cut-scene viewer.

Overall, Darksiders: Warmastered Edition rates a 7/10 for me. Here's how it could have been better;

  • 8/10- No cut-scene bug, or a la carte cut-scene viewing
  • 9/10- Easier method of switching between weapons/equips
  • 10/10- More upgrades\collectibles

With Darksiders out of the way, I was super excited about playing the sequel. It didn't take long for that excitement to die. This does NOT feel like a worthy successor to the first game in any way, shape, or form. Death spends most of his time acting like an angst-y smartass. His movements feel choppy and delayed. The environment reeks more of "Let's make a Warcraft game", and less of "biblically apocalyptic hell on earth". the dialogue from both Death, and the NPCs makes me feel like I am playing some medieval-themed RPG.

Now, with all criticisms aside, I haven't completed yet, so is a chance things get better. Even if they do though, it will be hard to wash the stench of what I have been playing out of my mouth, as this is not the Darksiders I was looking for.
